findings.text: Tee service duplicates content from an input pipe to an output pipe without copying page data, requiring distinct pipes and appropriate read and write modes, propagating nonblocking mode from either file, preparing both ends before linking, and reporting access and modification notifications when bytes are duplicated.
Tee entry validates the splice flag set, returns success for zero length, resolves both descriptors with bad descriptor on failure, and delegates to the tee service.

Splice entry returns immediately for zero length, rejects unknown splice flags, resolves input and output descriptors with bad descriptor on empty handles, and delegates to the shared splice dispatcher.

Vmsplice entry rejects unknown splice flags, resolves the descriptor, chooses source direction for writable files and destination direction for readable files with bad descriptor otherwise, imports the vector array with a small on stack fast path, returns zero for empty iterators, and dispatches to pipe fill or pipe drain helpers.

Shared splice dispatcher forbids explicit offsets alongside pipe ends, clears nowait state on pipe files, copies optional input and output offsets from user space with fault on failure, invokes the core splice engine, and copies updated offsets back with fault on failure while propagating engine errors.

Iterator to pipe helper packs user pages into pipe buffers in batches of sixteen, assigns user page operations and caller flags, splits spans across page boundaries, appends each chunk to the pipe, and on append failure reverts the iterator for the unfinished span, releases remaining pages in the batch, and returns accumulated bytes if any else the error.

Pipe to user path validates the pipe handle, clears nowait state, drains available pipe data under the pipe lock through a per buffer copy helper that faults on short copies, and reports access notification when bytes are moved.

User to pipe path maps the gift flag to the pipe buffer gift flag, validates the pipe handle, clears nowait state, waits for space under the pipe lock before filling from the iterator, and on success wakes readers and reports modification.

Input preparation succeeds fast when the pipe is nonempty and otherwise waits under lock while empty, aborting on pending signals, absent writers, or nonblocking mode; output preparation succeeds fast when not full and otherwise waits while full, signaling broken pipe when readers are gone and aborting on nonblocking mode or pending signals.

Pipe splice paths hold the pipe lock while waiting and while moving buffers, use a speculative lock free occupancy check before acquiring the lock, and order acquisition of two pipes by address to avoid deadlock between concurrent tee operations in opposite directions.

Pipe linking shares buffer descriptors from input tail to output head without copying data, acquires an extra reference on each shared buffer, clears gift and merge inheritance to prevent repeated page stealing, truncates the final buffer to the requested length, advances both indices, and wakes output readers when bytes were added.

Linking iterates until the requested length is satisfied, input is exhausted, output has no room, readers disappear, or a buffer reference cannot be taken, emitting broken pipe handling only when no progress was made and stopping with accumulated length otherwise.

Splice helpers translate missing output readers into a broken pipe signal plus pipe error, missing input writers into quiet termination of input wait, nonblocking mode into retryable busy status, pending signals into restartable interruption, and user copy or buffer acquisition failures into fault status.

Stacked filesystem helper copies size and block count from a lower inode to an upper inode while tolerating concurrent updates and thirty two bit tearing through appropriate read and write synchronization.
Stacked filesystem helper copies mode, ownership, device identity, all three timestamps, block size bits, flags, and link count from source to destination inode.

Size and block copying uses lock free size reads plus conditional spin protection: source block reads take the source lock only on wide counters, and destination updates take the destination lock when either size or block count is wider than a native word, avoiding nesting of size and block synchronization, with no extra cost on sixty four bit builds.
Statx attribute filler maps immutable and append inode flags to corresponding extended status attributes and marks the virtual filesystem flag subset as valid.

Atomic write filler always marks the atomic write result and attribute type as known, and only when a nonzero minimum unit is supplied it records minimum, maximum, optimal maximum, and a single segment limit and marks atomic writes as supported.

Virtual filesystem stat wrappers expose file descriptor, descriptor relative, current directory, and symlink following or nonfollowing variants that all converge on descriptor relative lookup with basic statistics and optional automount suppression.

Statx flag translation enables symlink following unless nofollow is requested and enables automount unless suppressed, while the path walk entry rejects any flag outside the supported nofollow, no automount, empty path, and sync type set.

Statx path helper performs attribute collection then records either the unique or legacy mount identifier with matching result bit and annotates mount roots while always marking that annotation as valid.
Descriptor relative stat performs lookup, attribute collection, and path release, and on stale handle it retries with revalidation enabled before returning the final status.

Old, new, and sixty four bit stat converters zero their destination, encode device identities, check inode number, link count, device validity, and thirty two bit size limits with overflow errors, map identifiers through munged namespace helpers, copy seconds and optional nanoseconds plus size block count and block size, and report user copy faults.

Stat system entries for old, new, and sixty four bit layouts resolve names, symlinks, descriptors, or descriptor relative names through the shared virtual filesystem helpers and then convert the kernel status record to the corresponding user layout.

Readlink helper rejects nonpositive sizes, looks up the path with empty path allowed, permits true symlinks and non symlink filesystems that provide a readlink operation, enforces readlink permission, updates access time, invokes the filesystem readlink, maps empty versus nonempty nonlink names to missing versus invalid errors, and retries stale handles with revalidation.

Stat and readlink paths bound old stat deprecation warnings to five initial reports, enforce overflow errors on truncated identifiers and large sizes, fault on failed user copies, and reject invalid readlink sizes and unsupported file types.

Observed application binary constants include splice control flags for nonblocking operation, gift ownership, and the full flag mask, file mode read and write bits plus nonblocking file status, extended status request and attribute bits for basic stats mount identifiers mount root immutable append and atomic writes, and descriptor relative and symlink lookup flags.
Pipe buffer acquisition delegates to the operation vector installed in the buffer, passing both pipe and buffer through to the type specific getter.

Splice descriptors observed here carry total length, remaining length, flags, and an iterator pointer, while pipe buffers carry page, offset, length, flags, and an operation vector, and pipe state exposes occupancy indices, limits, and reader and writer counts.

Kernel status records observed here carry device, inode number, mode, link count, ownership, device identity for special files, size, three timestamps, block count, block size, attribute and mask sets, mount identifiers, result mask, and atomic write limits.
